core_obligations: Reduce to showing that (1) implies (2), since (2) is the special case of (1) for finite separable extensions (proof line 8451).
Choose a surjective etale U -> X with U a scheme and pick a point p of Spec(A') x_X U over the closed point of Spec(A') (proof lines 8459-8464).
Lift p to a generalization p' over the generic point of Spec(A') and identify the corresponding point q' of Spec(K) x_X U with residue field a finite separable extension of K (proof lines 8465-8479).

Build the subring B of kappa(q') generated by the images of A and O_{U,u}, choose the prime q = B meet m with A meet q the maximal ideal of A, and apply the dominating valuation ring lemma to get A_1 (proof lines 8480-8505).
Translate the local ring map O_{U,u} -> A_1 into the morphism Spec(A_1) -> U -> X that completes the diagram, with fraction field kappa(q') finite separable over K (proof lines 8506-8517).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S, the existence part of the valuative criterion is equivalent to the same condition restricted to diagrams whose extension K' over K is finite separable (source lines 8436-8448). Only the direction (1) implies (2) needs work, and it is a real construction: from a surjective etale U -> X one takes a point p of Spec(A') x_X U over the closed point of Spec(A'), lifts it to a generalization p' over the generic point using that generalizations lift along flat morphisms, reads off a point q' of Spec(K) x_X U whose residue field is finite separable over K, forms the subring B of kappa(q') generated by A and the local ring O_{U,u}, chooses a prime q = B meet m with A meet q the maximal ideal of A, and applies the dominating valuation ring lemma to obtain the required A_1 contained in kappa(q').
